routes.name: Visa-free short stay (Schengen)
routes.summary: Many nationalities can visit Portugal without a visa for short stays under Schengen rules. Check the official lists to see if your passport is on it.

other: The exempt and visa-required nationality lists are on the official page but I could not read the list contents or the 90 in 180 day rule from it. Confirm there.

sources.label: Short stay visas: who needs a visa

routes.name: Schengen Short Stay Visa
routes.summary: Tourist or business visit visa for people whose nationality needs one. Apply with the Portuguese consulate or through the online visa portal.

other: Needs return booking, travel medical insurance, proof of funds and the last three bank statements, plus accommodation or an invitation.

documents: Passport valid more than 3 months after you leave
Work certificate, salary details and last three bank statements
Hotel booking or statement of responsibility, or other proof of purpose
routes.processing: Fee is not refunded if the visa is refused.

routes.name: Airport Transit Visa
routes.summary: Some nationalities need an airport transit visa even to change planes in a Portuguese airport without entering the country.

other: Official page has a section on airport transit visa requirements but the list was not readable. Check it for your nationality.

sources.label: Short stay visas: who needs a visa

routes.name: Seasonal Work Visa
routes.summary: Short stay visa for seasonal jobs in listed sectors. You need a work contract or offer from a Portuguese employer or temp work company.

other: Sectors: agriculture, livestock, forestry and fishing; hospitality; food, drink and tobacco industries; wholesale and retail; construction; land transport.
Needs decent accommodation, work accident insurance and medical cover.

documents: Work contract or offer with location, time, type of work, duration, salary and paid vacation

routes.name: Residency Visa for Employed Work
routes.summary: Residency visa for people with a job in Portugal. After arrival you apply to AIMA for a residence permit.

income.note: Base means of subsistence for 2026, net, first adult

other: Employment contract under Portuguese law and social security registration are required by the foreigners law text I read, which may be older than the 2025 changes.
Official base amount for long-stay visas is 920 EUR per month net in 2026 for the first adult, plus 50% for each extra adult and 30% for each child.

stay.note: The visa is valid 4 months with two entries. Then you apply to AIMA for a residence permit.

routes.processing: Official visa decision deadline is 60 days.

routes.name: Residency Visa for Highly Qualified Activity, Research or Teaching
routes.summary: Residency visa for researchers, teachers and highly qualified workers. The 2025 law changed how some work permit holders convert to this route.

other: Needs admission to a recognized research center or a qualifying contract, plus social security registration.
Details for this route were not on a readable official page. Check with the consulate.

routes.name: Qualified Job Seeker Visa
routes.summary: Old job seeker visa stopped on 23 October 2025. A new visa for qualified job seekers is set in the law but not open yet.

other: Consulates stopped accepting job seeker visa requests from 23 October 2025.
Applications for the new qualified version can only be made after it is regulated. No date given.
The law says it is for people with specialized technical skills, with an appointment within 120 days. Skills list is still to come.

routes.name: Residency Visa for Independent Work or Entrepreneur
routes.summary: Residency visa for freelancers and business owners. You need a company, registered self-employment or a service contract.

income.note: Base means of subsistence for 2026, net, first adult

other: Must be registered with tax and social security and qualified for the activity where required.

routes.name: Entrepreneur and Startup Residence
routes.summary: Residence permit for people running an entrepreneurial project, including an innovative startup in a certified incubator.

other: The law waives one general residence requirement for these applicants. Startup visa page had no details, so conditions are unconfirmed.

routes.name: Residency or Temporary Stay Visa for Remote Work (Digital Nomad)
routes.summary: Visa for people who work remotely for clients or employers abroad. There is a temporary stay version and a residency version.

other: Official pages list this visa but do not show its own income threshold or documents. Do not assume the general amount applies.
Official base amount for long-stay visas is 920 EUR per month net in 2026 for the first adult, plus 50% for each extra adult and 30% for each child.

routes.name: Residency Visa for Retirees and Passive Income
routes.summary: Residency visa for retirees and people living on passive income. Listed as a fixed residency purpose.

other: Official pages do not give the passive income amount for this visa.
Official base amount for long-stay visas is 920 EUR per month net in 2026 for the first adult, plus 50% for each extra adult and 30% for each child.

routes.name: Residence Permit for Investment (ARI, Golden Visa)
routes.summary: Residence permit for investors. Amounts and eligible investment types are not confirmed here, so check AIMA's ARI portal.

other: AIMA pages were blocked to automated reading, so amounts, minimum stay days and current eligible investment types are unconfirmed.
Family reunification rules waive the usual 2 year wait for holders of this permit type.

routes.name: Study and Research Visa
routes.summary: Residency visa for study, research, exchanges, internships and volunteering. Temporary stay version exists for shorter courses.

other: Higher education students need proof of enrollment, paid tuition, means of subsistence and health coverage, per the law text I read.
Residence permit for students is valid one year and renewable, per the same text. Confirm current rules.

routes.name: Youth Mobility Visa (Working Holiday)
routes.summary: Temporary stay visa for young people from countries that have a youth mobility memorandum with Portugal. Stay is up to 12 months and cannot be extended.

other: Work, training or study is allowed as a secondary activity. Age limits are not stated on the page, so check the memorandum for your country.

routes.name: CPLP Mobility Visa
routes.summary: Visa for citizens of CPLP countries under the CPLP Mobility Agreement signed in Luanda on 17 July 2021. It has lighter financial proof rules.

other: Applies to nationals of states where the agreement is in force. The page does not list them.
Financial proof can be replaced by a host entity responsibility term, a signed term from a resident, or admission to higher education.

routes.name: Family Reunification
routes.summary: A resident can bring family members who live abroad. First the sponsor asks AIMA, then the family applies for a residency visa.

other: Sponsor needs a residence permit valid for at least 2 years, or 15 months for a spouse who lived with them 18 months before they entered Portugal.
The 2 year rule does not apply to dependent minors, and holders of investment and some other permits are exempt.
Sponsor needs adequate housing and enough income without social benefits.
Spouses must both be at least 18. Family must take Portuguese language and constitutional values training.
AIMA decision is due within 9 months, extendable in complex cases.

steps: Sponsor asks AIMA for family reunification
After a favorable decision, family applies for a residency visa at a consulate
routes.processing: Law sets 9 months for the AIMA decision.

routes.name: Permanent Residence Permit
routes.summary: Permanent residence after years on a temporary permit. Law text I read says 5 years, basic Portuguese, no long sentences, housing and income.

other: Text read is the AIMA copy of Law 23/2007 and may predate the 2025 changes. Confirm current years with AIMA.
Needs at least 5 years of temporary residence, no prison sentence over one year in the last 5 years, means of subsistence and housing.

routes.name: EU, EEA and Swiss Free Movement
routes.summary: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens do not need a long-stay visa to live in Portugal, and neither do their family members. They register once they stay past 3 months.

other: Official page confirms exemption from the long-stay visa. Registration steps and permanent residence timing could not be read, so confirm with AIMA.

sources.label: National visas: who needs a visa

routes.name: Asylum and International Protection
routes.summary: You must be in Portugal to apply. Go to AIMA's reception center in Lisbon, the police, or tell border police at the airport.

other: You cannot apply from abroad or at an embassy.

steps: Say you want to apply for asylum
Get a declaration valid 60 days, renewable
Wait for the admissibility decision (30 working days, 7 at a border)
If admitted, get a provisional residence permit valid 6 months, renewable
routes.processing: AIMA admissibility decision in 30 working days.

routes.name: Citizenship by Naturalization
routes.summary: Portuguese citizenship after 7 years of legal residence for EU and Portuguese-speaking country (CPLP) nationals, 10 years for everyone else. New rules apply from 19 May 2026.

citizenship.note: 7 years for EU and CPLP nationals. Law does not make you give up another nationality, but confirm with IRN.

routes.name: Citizenship by Marriage or Partnership
routes.summary: Spouses of Portuguese citizens can apply after more than 3 years of marriage. Partners can apply after 3 years once a court recognizes the union.

other: Same disqualifiers as naturalization apply (convictions, security risks).
Opposition is not possible if the marriage or union lasts more than 6 years or there are common Portuguese children.
Some tests such as language requirements may apply under the new rules. Confirm with IRN.

citizenship.note: Portuguese law does not require giving up another nationality.

routes.name: Citizenship by Descent
routes.summary: Grandchildren of Portuguese-born citizens can claim by declaration if they have real ties to Portugal. Great-grandchildren can also qualify. Sephardic and community-of-origin routes were removed.

other: Grandchild route needs effective ties to the national community and the same language, history and conduct checks as naturalization.
Sources disagree on residence years for great-grandchildren, one says 5 years of legal residence. Confirm with IRN.
Cases filed before 19 May 2026 follow the old rules.

routes.name: Citizenship for Children Born in Portugal
routes.summary: Child born in Portugal to foreign parents can get citizenship if at least one parent has had 5 years of legal residence.

other: Source mentions 5 years at time of birth, plus regular school attendance where applicable, in two different articles. Confirm exact conditions with IRN.
